title: Riverbend Patient Financial Services Policy: Balances That May Be Enrolled in a Patient Payment Plan
content:
**Rule.** Only the patient's own self-pay balances that are already billed to the patient are enrolled in a **Patient Payment Plan**. An encounter balance may be enrolled only while its hospital account is in patient due status — a condition read from the hospital account itself, account by account, at the time of enrollment.

**Balances that stay out.**
- A balance still awaiting insurance adjudication (insurance pending) is never enrolled.
- An account on billing hold for a charge dispute or a good-faith-estimate dispute is not enrolled until the dispute is resolved.
- A balance placed with the collection agency must first be recalled.

**Amount and repeat enrollment.** The amount enrolled is the account's patient balance on the enrollment date. An encounter is enrolled at most once in the same plan; a later increase on an enrolled account (a late charge or a new patient-responsibility posting) is enrolled as an add-on on its own date.

### Account-by-account reading

| Hospital account | Enrolled? |
|---|---|
| Patient due, no hold, not with the agency | Yes, at its patient balance on the enrollment date |
| Insurance pending | No |
| On a charge-dispute or good-faith-estimate-dispute billing hold | Not until the dispute is resolved |
| Placed with the collection agency | Only once recalled |

**Hypothetical.** An account enrolled at 300.00 later takes a 40.00 late charge; the 40.00 is enrolled as an add-on on the date it is enrolled, and the account itself is not enrolled a second time.
